title: Isolation of human ESC-derived cardiac derivatives and embryonic heart cells for RNA-seq analysis
author: Santoro, Chien, et al.
materials:
Following the in vitro cardiac differentiation as noted above, a variety of hESC-derived cardiac subpopulations that involve early MCPs to cardiac intermediates and differentiated cardiac cells can be isolated at different time points. During differentiation, ISL1+ cardiac progenitors first appear on day 3 and peak by day 6 when ISL1+ cells occupy 80%–90% of the total differentiated cells. These cells mainly differentiate into beating cardiomyocytes along with generating small subsets of other differentiated cell types, such as pacemaker, smooth muscle, and endothelial cells from day 8–10 onward. The isolation of the hESC-derived cardiac subpopulations is conducted using fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS) and lineage-specific markers’ antibodies for cell staining on days 3 (for MCPs), 6 (for cardiac intermediates), and 10 (for differentiated cardiac cells) of the differentiation, respectively (Figures 1 and 2).10.On each of the specified days (i.e., days 3, 6, and 10 of cardiac differentiation):a.Aspirate the old medium on the differentiation 12-well plates and wash the cells with DPBS once.b.Add 0.5 mL of Accutase to each well of the 12-well plate. steps.title: Prepare cells for FACS
steps.instruction: On differentiation days 3, 6, and 10 aspirate old medium from each well of the 12‑well plate, wash once with DPBS, add 0.5 mL Accutase, incubate 5–10 min at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂; add 0.5 mL mTeSR1 or FBS, gently pipette to collect cells into a 15‑mL conical tube, centrifuge 200 × g for 5 min at 20–25 °C, aspirate supernatant, resuspend in 100 µL DPBS, count cells, centrifuge again (200 × g, 5 min, 20–25 °C), aspirate, and resuspend in Blocking/Staining Solution A at 1–2 × 10⁶ cells per 100–200 µL. Divide the suspension into separate 1.5 mL tubes for unstained control, single‑color controls, and multicolor‑stained samples.

steps.title: Block cells before staining
steps.instruction: Incubate all tubes on a shaker at 4 °C for 15 min in Blocking/Staining Solution A.

steps.title: Stain surface markers
steps.instruction: Centrifuge 200 × g for 5 min (20–25 °C), aspirate supernatant, resuspend each tube in 100–200 µL primary‑antibody mix prepared in Blocking/Staining Solution A (see Table 1 for antibodies and dilutions, e.g., PDGFRα‑AF647 1:100, CD31‑APC 1:150, HCN4‑PE 1:200, etc.), incubate on shaker at 4 °C for 30–60 min, centrifuge 200 × g 5 min, wash with 300 µL DPBS, repeat wash, then aspirate.

steps.title: Choose staining pathway
steps.instruction: If no intracellular staining or secondary antibody is required, resuspend cells in 300 µL FACS buffer, filter into a 5 mL FACS tube, keep on ice (proceed to step 18). If the primary antibody is unconjugated, add fluorochrome‑conjugated secondary antibody (1:500–1:1 000 in 500–1 000 µL Blocking/Staining Solution A), shake 4 °C 15 min, then repeat the surface‑staining washes and continue to step 12a or 12c. If intracellular staining is needed (as for ISL1), proceed to step 13.

steps.title: Fix cells for intracellular staining
steps.instruction: Add 4 % paraformaldehyde (PFA) to the cell suspension, shake at 20–25 °C for 20–25 min, wrap tubes in aluminum foil and protect from light.

steps.title: Add RNase inhibitor to buffers
steps.instruction: Supplement all buffers and solutions used after fixation (steps 13–18) with RNase inhibitor (e.g., RNaseOUT) at 1:100 (v/v) to protect RNA.

steps.title: Permeabilize and block intracellularly
steps.instruction: Centrifuge cells 400 × g for 5 min (20–25 °C), aspirate, resuspend in 1 mL Permeabilization solution, repeat centrifugation, then resuspend in 0.5 mL Blocking/Staining Solution B; incubate on shaker at 4 °C for 15 min (wrap in foil).

steps.title: Stain intracellular markers
steps.instruction: Centrifuge 400 × g 5 min, aspirate, resuspend in 100–200 µL primary‑antibody mix prepared in Blocking/Staining Solution B (e.g., ISL1 1:100, OCT3/4 1:50, etc.), incubate on shaker at 4 °C for 30–60 min, centrifuge 400 × g 5 min, wash with 300 µL PBS, repeat wash, then aspirate.

steps.title: Apply secondary antibodies
steps.instruction: Resuspend cells in 500–1 000 µL Blocking/Staining Solution B containing fluorochrome‑conjugated secondary antibody (dilution 1:500–1:1 000), shake at 4 °C for 15 min, centrifuge 400 × g 5 min, wash twice with 300 µL PBS (centrifuge each wash 400 × g 5 min), finally centrifuge, aspirate, resuspend in 300 µL FACS buffer, filter into a 5 mL FACS tube and keep on ice.

steps.title: Prepare FACS controls
steps.instruction: In addition to unstained and single‑color controls, prepare isotype‑primary‑antibody controls, secondary‑only controls, and positive/negative cell‑type controls (e.g., undifferentiated hESCs).

steps.title: Sort cardiac subpopulations
steps.instruction: Run samples on a FACSARIA III (100 µm nozzle) at 4 °C, flow rate 800–1 200 events / s. Set PMT voltages with unstained and single‑color controls, gate singlets (FSC‑A vs SSC‑A, FSC‑W vs FSC‑H, SSC‑W vs SSC‑H), exclude debris and doublets, and for live sorting gate DAPI‑ or PI‑negative cells. Define sorting gates using isotype and marker‑positive controls. Sort ISL1⁺PDGFRα⁺ MCPs (day 3), ISL1⁺Lin⁺ cardiac intermediates (day 6), and ISL1⁻Lin⁺ differentiated cardiac cells (day 10) into pre‑coated 1.5 mL tubes containing 100 µL PBS; collect ≥10 000 (preferably ≥20 000) cells per population. Immediately centrifuge tubes at 400 × g for 5 min at 4 °C and aspirate supernatant.

steps.title: Protease digestion of sorted cells
steps.instruction: Clean bench with RNase‑Zap. Resuspend each cell pellet (from step 12) in 100 µL Digestion Buffer plus 4 µL Protease (RecoverAll kit) in a 1.5 mL tube, incubate at 50 °C for 1 h. Optionally snap‑freeze lysates at –80 °C for 2–4 weeks.

steps.title: Isolate RNA with RecoverAll kit
steps.instruction: Combine 120 µL Isolation Additive with 275 µL 100 % ethanol; add 395 µL of this mixture to the lysate, mix, load onto a filter cartridge, centrifuge 10 000 × g for 30 s, discard flow‑through. Add 700 µL Wash 1, centrifuge 10 000 × g 30 s, discard. Add 500 µL Wash 2/3, centrifuge 10 000 × g 30 s, discard; repeat Wash 2/3 once more. Spin the assembly at 10 000 × g for an additional 30 s to remove residual fluid.

steps.title: DNase treatment of RNA
steps.instruction: Prepare DNase mix: 4 µL DNase, 6 µL 10× DNase buffer, 50 µL nuclease‑free water. Add 60 µL mix to the center of the filter cartridge, cap, incubate 30 min at 20–25 °C. Add 700 µL Wash 1, incubate 60 s, centrifuge 10 000 × g 30 s. Add 500 µL Wash 2/3, centrifuge 10 000 × g 30 s; repeat Wash 2/3. Spin 10 000 × g for 1 min to dry the filter.

steps.title: Elute and quantify RNA
steps.instruction: Transfer the filter cartridge to a fresh collection tube, apply 20–60 µL Elution Solution (or nuclease‑free water) at 20–25 °C to the center, incubate 1 min, centrifuge 1 min at maximum speed; collect eluate containing RNA. Measure RNA integrity and concentration with Agilent RNA 6000 Nano kit on a Bioanalyzer 2100. Store RNA at –80 °C for 2–4 weeks before cDNA library construction.

steps.title: Dissect embryonic/fetal hearts
steps.instruction: Immediately after surgery place human embryonic/fetal hearts (4.5–10 weeks gestation) into 35 mm dishes containing 5 mL DMEM/F12 on ice. Under a hood, dissect each heart into outflow tract, ventricle, and atria, removing fat and connective tissue, and transfer each compartment into separate 35 mm dishes with 5 mL Heart‑Primary solution on ice.

steps.title: Enzymatic digestion of heart tissue
steps.instruction: Cut each region into the smallest possible pieces, transfer pieces to separate 15 mL tubes containing 3 mL Collagenase A (freshly prepared). Pre‑digest in a 37 °C shaking water bath for 10 min, centrifuge 200 × g 3 min, discard supernatant. Add 3 mL Collagenase B, tap gently, then digest in a 37 °C shaking water bath for 25 min (if no shaker, manually shake 1 min every 5 min).

steps.title: Filter and collect single cells
steps.instruction: Pass each digestion suspension through a 40‑µm cell strainer into a new 50 mL tube containing 1 mL FBS to neutralize. If visible tissue remains, add another 3 mL Collagenase B to the original tube, repeat the 25‑min digestion, and combine supernatants. Centrifuge 200 × g 3 min, discard supernatant.

steps.title: Manual single‑cell picking
steps.instruction: Resuspend the cell pellet in 200 µL Cell‑Suspension Buffer (TrypLE Express + DPBS 1:1). Transfer to a 35 mm dish, pick individual cells with a micro‑capillary pipette (~0.3 µL) and deposit each into a 0.2‑mL thin‑walled PCR tube containing 2 µL Cell Lysis Buffer (nuclease‑free water + 0.2 % Triton X‑100 + 2 U/µL RNase inhibitor), 1 µL 10 µM oligo‑dT primer (5′‑AAGCAGTGGTATCAACGCAGAGTACT30VN‑3′), and 1 µL 10 mM dNTP mix. Snap‑freeze tubes on dry ice and store at –80 °C for 2–4 weeks.

steps.title: FACS single‑cell sorting
steps.instruction: Resuspend cells in 300 µL FACS buffer, filter into a 5 mL FACS tube, keep on ice. Using a cell sorter (e.g., FACSARIA III) and following the gating strategy of step 18b, sort DAPI‑ or PI‑negative live cells one per well into 96‑ or 384‑well plates pre‑loaded with 2 µL Cell Lysis Buffer, 1 µL 10 µM oligo‑dT primer, and 1 µL 10 mM dNTP mix (plates prepared in advance and stored at –20 °C). After sorting, snap‑freeze plates on dry ice and store at –80 °C for 2–4 weeks before cDNA library construction.
